title: Does an Executable Emulator Validator Reduce Semantic Failures in LLM-Generated Network Configuration Changes?
abstract: We report a fully preregistered paired experiment (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) that tested whether inserting an executable emulator validator into a generate→validate→repair pipeline reduces semantic/network-level failures versus an LLM-only suggestion workflow. Using a deterministic paired design with N=120 intent→configuration tasks (40 per topology class: edge, core, leaf–spine) we produced one shared initial candidate per task via gpt-5-mini (model_calls_used = 120) and evaluated the identical candidate under both conditions. The guarded pipeline used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0) with at most one repair iteration per guarded episode. Observed outcomes: baseline successes = 120/120; guarded successes = 120/120; paired contingency: n_11=120, n_10=0, n_01=0, n_00=0. Exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired-difference estimate = 0.00; paired-bootstrap-percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Validator traces record repair_applied = false for every guarded episode. We expand methodological detail, representative diagnostics grounded in archived validator traces and task manifests, reproducibility guidance tied to the preregistered artifacts, and discuss construct/external validity limits and design recommendations for future confirmatory studies.

sections.introduction:
Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as operator assistants that translate high-level intent into device-level configuration commands for network operations (NetOps). However, syntactically plausible command sequences can violate temporal and stateful workflow invariants (e.g., make-before-break, required shutdown sequences) and produce semantic failures that only become visible in closed-loop execution. Prior work therefore proposes tool-augmented pipelines that interpose deterministic verification, emulation, or veto layers to detect or correct such semantic errors before enactment. Measuring the marginal contribution of these validators requires experimental designs that target stateful and temporal invariants rather than only token- or syntax-level correctness.

We executed a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) that isolates the validator/repair subsystem's marginal effect by scoring the exact same generator output under both a baseline (LLM-only) and a guarded (executable validator ± bounded repair) condition. The mechanistic research question was: does integrating an executable network emulator as a validator in a generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce semantic/network-level failures when enacting LLM-generated configuration changes compared to an LLM-only suggestion workflow? The run produced a ceiling outcome (100% baseline success), which is itself an informative scientific result because it shows how generator calibration, task selection, and paired shared-generation designs interact to determine whether repairs are empirically exercised. Below we expand the methodological rationale, report concrete numeric outcomes grounded in archived artifacts, present representative per-episode diagnostics, and discuss the practical implications and prespecified follow-up recommendations.
sections.related_work:
Executable, emulation-grounded benchmarks and tool-integrated evaluations have shown that static or syntax-focused metrics miss important closed-loop failure classes such as make-before-break violations, group-availability breaches, and order-dependent invariants. Recent benchmark and tool papers demonstrate that integrating executable checks or deterministic emulation can detect and sometimes prevent semantic errors produced by generative models (see, e.g., Protogeros et al.; NetConfArena; Aether). Survey and prototype studies also advocate bounded-autonomy guardrails—veto layers, canaries, and generate→validate→repair pipelines—as practical safety measures for agentic NetOps deployments. These works collectively establish two points motivating our confirmatory design: (1) closed-loop executable tests reveal failure modes not captured by text-only metrics, and (2) deterministic verification can materially reduce enacted semantic errors in contexts where generators produce invalid candidates.

Methodological critiques in the literature note that generator sampling variance often confounds verification efficacy when distinct generator draws are used per condition. Paired shared-generation designs avoid that confound by evaluating identical outputs across conditions, but they sacrifice the ability to observe repair behavior when the generator and prompts produce already-valid candidates. Our study complements the prior literature by operationalizing this trade-off within a fully preregistered confirmatory protocol and by archiving fine-grained validator traces that permit mechanistic diagnosis of degenerate (ceiling) outcomes.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. The experiment was preregistered (CNSM2026-A-prereg-v1) and executed according to a paired-binary confirmatory plan. The study used a deterministic paired design with exactly N=120 distinct intent→configuration tasks, deterministically partitioned into three topology classes (edge, core, leaf–spine) of 40 tasks each. The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, with the prespecified confirmatory test the exact two-sided McNemar test and a paired-bootstrap-percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). The preregistration fixed the repair budget (≤1 repair per guarded episode), deterministic reset and contamination checks, and an explicit missingness/exclusion plan.

Task corpus and payload schema. Tasks were produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and encoded: initial_state, expected_final_state, a natural-language intent, an explicit required_sequence, and difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count, level). Workflow_policies (for example, must_be_down_for_fields, final_group_constraints, and make-before-break patterns) were expressed as machine-checkable constraints in the payload and enforced by the validator at execution time. Representative required_command_count values in the manifest ranged from 2 to 6 and difficulty levels include medium, hard, and very_hard.

Shared-generation paired protocol and generator configuration. For each pair the harness issued one shared generation call to the declared model (gpt-5-mini) and reused that identical candidate for both baseline and guarded scoring. Model-level accounting in the execution manifest: model_calls_used = 120, hosted_model_call_event_count = 120, cache_miss_count = 120, cache_hit_count = 0. The paired design eliminates generator variance across conditions so any discordance must stem from validator/repair behavior.

Validator and repair semantics. The guarded pipeline invoked deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0). For each guarded episode the validator: (a) executed the shared candidate in a seeded emulator initialized from the task's initial_state, (b) checked workflow_policies encoded in the task payload as executable invariants, and (c) emitted a structured validator_trace containing validation_before, validation_after, observed_touched_field_count, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_count, violation_codes, and repair_applied. The preregistered repair policy permitted at most one repair iteration when validator.violation_count > 0 and would archive repair-provider-call traces if any repairs were requested or applied. In the executed run validator.violation_count = 0 and validator.repair_applied = false for every guarded episode; consequently no repair-provider-call artifacts were produced.

Instrumentation and contamination controls. The harness enforced deterministic emulator resets between tasks, container checksum verification, duplicate-output detection, and cross-condition cache-key reuse detection. Deterministic reconciliation reported complete_pair_count = 120; planned_episode_count = 240; completed_episode_count = 240; failed_episode_count = 0; and all deterministic consistency checks passed. Contamination checks did not flag any episodes.

Scoring and prespecified analysis. Each paired observation produced a binary semantic outcome (pass = emulator-observed final_state satisfied the task's expected_final_state and required_sequence constraints under scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation; fail otherwise). The preregistered confirmatory analysis used exact two-sided McNemar and the paired-bootstrap-percentile 95% CI with 10,000 resamples and seed 1729. The preregistered power calculation assumed a baseline failure ≈ 0.40 and targeted an absolute reduction of 0.15; we report that assumption and show how the observed baseline violates that planning assumption.
sections.results:
Execution summary and primary outcome. The run completed without technical exclusions. Condition-level summaries from the analysis artifacts: baseline successes = 120, baseline failures = 0; guarded successes = 120, guarded failures = 0. The paired contingency table (analysis artifact) is n_11 = 120, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Exact two-sided McNemar p-value = 1.0; paired-difference point estimate = 0.00. The preregistered paired-bootstrap-percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.00, 0.00]. Validator traces record repair_applied = false for every guarded episode, so no repair-provider-call artifacts were produced.

Representative per-task diagnostics. Representative task-manifest and validator-trace values (archived artifacts) illustrate the kinds of stateful checks exercised even when validation passes. Examples (all values come from archived per-episode validator traces): task-000001 (pattern shutdown_configure_restore) parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4, observed_touched_field_count = 3, validation_after.valid = true, violation_count = 0; task-000002 (pattern make_before_break_uplink_switchover) parsed_command_count = 2, required_command_count = 2, observed_touched_field_count = 2, validation_after.valid = true, violation_count = 0; task-000003 (pattern paired_link_atomic_mtu_change) parsed_command_count = 6, required_command_count = 6, observed_touched_field_count = 4, validation_after.valid = true, violation_count = 0. Successes were uniform across topology classes (Edge: 40/40; Core: 40/40; Leaf–spine: 40/40).

Diagnostic provenance and deterministic accounting. Analysis artifacts record complete_pair_count = 120 and provider-call audit values hosted_model_call_event_count = 120, cache_miss_count = 120, cache_hit_count = 0, and stage_counts shows 120 shared_initial_generation events. Contamination and missingness summaries are empty of flags or exclusions. These artifacts document that the shared generator outputs satisfied the encoded workflow_policies and required sequences so the guard had no corrective actions to apply.

Statistical interpretation. The confirmatory McNemar test returns p = 1.0 because there were zero discordant pairs (n_10 = n_01 = 0). The paired-bootstrap CI is degenerate at [0.00, 0.00] under the prespecified resampling scheme because every resample reproduces the same paired contingency when no discordant pairs exist. The preregistered power calculation assumed baseline failure ≈ 0.40; the observed baseline = 0.00 violates that assumption and renders the originally targeted effect-size power calculation inapplicable for this execution.
sections.discussion:
Interpreting a ceiling outcome. The key scientific implication is that the paired shared-generation design successfully isolates validator/repair marginal effects: because gpt-5-mini under the frozen prompt strategy produced valid candidates for the curated task bank, the validator observed zero violations and did not exercise repairs. This ceiling outcome is a valid and informative result: it documents that for this synthetic corpus and the declared model/prompt the guard was idle. It does not contradict prior findings that validators reduce enacted errors when generators err; rather it highlights how experimental design choices (shared-generation vs independent draws, task difficulty distribution, prompt calibration) determine whether repair policies can be empirically exercised.

Design trade-offs, operational recommendations, and prespecified follow-ups. The run makes explicit a practical trade-off between internal validity and the ability to exercise repair behavior. Recommendations grounded in the preregistered plan and archived artifacts include: (1) run an independent-generation arm (one generator draw per condition) to observe guard interventions at the cost of reintroducing generator variance, (2) prespecified prompt perturbations on a subset of tasks to increase generator-induced violation incidence while preserving paired blocks for internal control, (3) enrich task stratification toward higher dependency-rule counts and very_hard levels to raise the probability of generator mistakes, and (4) exploratory arms with an expanded repair budget (>1 repair iteration) to measure repair convergence and provider-call costs when repairs occur. Each recommendation was anticipated in the preregistration and is actionable using the same harness and artifact schema.

What the artifacts add to auditability. Even when unused, a deterministic executable validator that emits structured traces (checked rules, touched fields, violation_codes, repair_applied flags) materially improves post-hoc auditability and failure diagnosis. The archived validator traces and deterministic reconciliation provide transparent accounting of model usage, staged events, and why repairs were not triggered. Such artifact-rich records enable reproducible follow-up experiments that relax the shared-generation constraint or vary generator families while preserving identical executable tests.

Threats to validity and scope. Internal validity for this execution is high: deterministic provisioning, exhaustive provider-call audits, no technical exclusions, and reproducible validator traces. Construct validity is limited because workflow_policies and task payloads are synthetic encodings that do not capture full vendor heterogeneity or partial telemetry observability; some real-world failure modes may therefore be absent. External validity is constrained by the synthetic deterministic task corpus, a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini), and a frozen prompting strategy. Statistical conclusion validity is affected by the ceiling: observed baseline = 0.00 invalidates the preregistered power assumptions (targeted absolute reduction = 0.15) and makes the McNemar confirmatory test uninformative for the originally targeted effect size. All these limitations are documented in the preregistration and archived artifacts.
sections.conclusion: In a fully preregistered paired experiment (N=120) comparing an executable generate→validate→repair pipeline against an LLM-only workflow under a deterministic harness with gpt-5-mini, every shared initial candidate satisfied the emulator's required_sequence and workflow_policies. The experiment produced n_11 = 120, a paired-difference estimate of 0.00 (exact McNemar p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00], 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), and validator.repair_applied = false in all guarded episodes. Scientifically, the result documents a ceiling for this curated synthetic task bank and illustrates how a shared-generation paired design isolates validator/repair effects but can mask repair benefits when the generator is well-calibrated for the chosen corpus. Methodologically, we show that preregistered, artifact-rich paired designs combined with executable validators that emit fine-grained traces permit reproducible diagnosis of degenerate confirmatory outcomes and support principled follow-up designs (independent condition generation, prompt perturbations, harder tasks, and expanded repair budgets) to quantify practical repair utility under realistic generator variance.

limitations: Confirmatory scope: results are narrowly scoped to the preregistered synthetic task set, a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini), and a frozen prompting strategy; generalization to production heterogeneity is limited.
Synthetic task provenance: tasks were synthetic/deterministic and may underrepresent noisy, adversarial, or multi-vendor production incidents; external validity to live networks is constrained.

Shared-generation design: using a single shared initial generation per paired task isolates validator/repair efficacy but precludes detection of generation-variance effects; this choice contributed to the ceiling outcome and limits inference about repair utility on independently generated invalid outputs.

Validator fidelity: the deterministic emulator/validator is reproducible but simplifies heterogeneity present in multi-vendor, partially observable production environments; some real-world failure modes may not be exposed.

Statistical ceiling: baseline success reached 100% on the tested task bank, violating the preregistered power assumptions (targeted absolute reduction = 0.15) and rendering the McNemar confirmatory test uninformative for demonstrating the preregistered effect size.
